Halo, teknisi! Aku NOVA, asisten laboratorium ini. Kita punya masalah besar. Automatic Watering System tiba-tiba berhenti bekerja!

content.text:
Halo, teknisi! Aku NOVA, asisten laboratorium ini. Kita punya masalah besar. Automatic Watering System tiba-tiba berhenti bekerja!

objects.name: TeksKedua
objects.string:
Pertama, kita harus memastikan perangkatnya berfungsi. Setelah itu, kita pulihkan koneksi jaringan dan terakhir memperbaiki aturan otomatisasinya.

events.comment: Dialogue stage machine. DialogueStage: 0 = typing first page, 1 = first page done (waiting Enter), 2 = typing second page, 3 = second page done (waiting Enter), 4 = dialogue closed.
Setup: keep the full texts aside (the objects are overwritten by the typewriter), freeze the player, show the panel and dim the scene.
Page 1 typewriter: reveal TypeProgress characters (42 per second).
Page 1 fully typed: Enter switches to page 2 (Enter is ignored while DialogueStage is 0).
Page 2 typewriter, same effect.
Page 2 fully typed: Enter closes the dialogue, removes the dimming and gives the player control back.
Hide the white markers but keep their collision detection active.
While any part of the player overlaps jalan, remember this safe spot. Otherwise revert, so restricted areas are never entered.
SmoothCamera follows the player; clamp the view inside background (-393,-283,2019x1250) for a 1280x720 view.

tests.description: Verify the mission introduction dialogue: dimming, typewriter on both pages, Enter locked while typing, movement frozen then restored
tests.name: mission_dialogue_sequence
source: // --- Stage 0: dialogue open, first page typing ---
harness.assert(obj('panel') && obj('panel').hidden === false, 'panel is visible at scene start');
harness.assert(obj('TeksKedua').hidden === true, 'TeksKedua is hidden at scene start');
// --- Enter must NOT advance while typing ---
harness.assert(stage() === 0, 'Enter does not advance while page 1 is still typing');
harness.assert(obj('TeksKedua').hidden === true, 'TeksKedua still hidden after Enter during typing');
harness.assert(obj('TeksPertama').hidden === false, 'TeksPertama still visible after Enter during typing');
// --- Player movement frozen while dialogue is open ---
`Player is frozen during dialogue (moved ${(frozenX - startX).toFixed(2)},${(frozenY - startY).toFixed(2)})`);
const done1 = await harness.stepUntil(() => stage() >= 1, { maxFrames: 900 });
harness.assert(done1, 'Page 1 finished typing on its own');
harness.assert(t2early.length < full1.length, `Page 2 starts typing from the beginning (${t2early.length} chars)`);
// --- Enter still locked while page 2 types ---
harness.assert(stage() === 2, 'Enter does not close while page 2 is still typing');
harness.assert(obj('panel').hidden === false, 'panel still visible while page 2 types');
const done2 = await harness.stepUntil(() => stage() >= 3, { maxFrames: 900 });
harness.assert(done2, 'Page 2 finished typing on its own');
harness.assert(obj('DimOverlay').hidden === true, 'DimOverlay (background dimming) removed after closing');
const moved = await harness.stepUntil(() => Math.abs(obj('NewSprite').x - closeX) > 5, { maxFrames: 90 });
harness.assert(moved, `Player can move again after dialogue (x ${closeX.toFixed(1)} -> ${obj('NewSprite').x.toFixed(1)})`);

eventsFunctionsExtensions.shortDescription: Smoothly scroll to follow an object.
description: The camera follows an object according to:
- a frame rate independent catch-up speed to make the scrolling from smooth to strong
- a maximum speed to do linear following ([open the project online](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?project=example://platformer-with-tilemap)) or slow down the camera when teleporting the object
- a follow-free zone to avoid scrolling on small movements
- an offset to see further in one direction
- an extra delay and catch-up speed to give an impression of speed (useful for dash)
- position forecasting and delay to simulate a cameraman response time
A platformer dedicated behavior allows to switch of settings when the character is in air or on the floor. This can be used to stabilize the camera when jumping.

events.comment:
Delaying and forecasting can be used at the same time.
Forecasting only use the positions that are older than the one used for delaying.
The behavior uses a position history that is split in 2 arrays:
- one for delaying the position (from TimeFromStart to TimeFromStart - CamearDelay)
- one for forecasting the position (from TimeFromStart - CamearDelay to TimeFromStart - CamearDelay - ForecastHistoryDuration

At each frame, the camera must catchup the target by a given ratio (speed)
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1) - targetX) * speed

The frame rate must not impact on the catch-up speed, we don't want a speed in ratio per frame but a speed ratio per second, like this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1s) - targetX) * speed

Ok, but we still need to process each frame, we can use a exponent for this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * speed^timeDelta
cameraX(t) = targetX + (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * exp(timeDelta * ln(speed))

pow is probably more efficient than precalculated log if the speed is changed continuously but this might be rare enough.

events.comment:
Simple linear regression
y = A * x + B

A = Covariance / VarianceX
B = MeanY - A * MeanX

Note than we could use only one position every N positions to reduce the process time,
but if we really need efficient process JavaScript and circular queues are a must.

VarianceX = sum((X[i] - MeanX)²)
VarianceY = sum((Y[i] - MeanY)²)
Covariance = sum((X[i] - MeanX) * (Y[i] - MeanY))

y = A * x + B

A = Covariance / VarianceX
B = MeanY - A * MeanX
Axis permutation to avoid a ratio between 2 numbers near 0.
Permute back axis

events.comment:
Perpendicular line:
pA = -1/a; 
pB = -pA * x + y

Intersection:
/ ProjectedY = a * ProjectedX + b
\ ProjectedY = pA * ProjectedX + b

Solution that is cleaned out from indeterminism (like 0 / 0 or infinity / infinity):
ProjectedX= (x + (y - b) * a) / (a² + 1)
ProjectedY = y + (x * a - y + b) / (a² + 1)
